newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels want African force, oppose French.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels want African force, oppose French.

text.p: Rebels holding a swathe of eastern Zaire said on Wednesday they wanted an African force to protect refugees and opposed French troops intervening in the region.

"I don't know why the French have to intervene here again for humanitarian purposes because we have declared a ceasefire," Laurent Kabila, spokesman for the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told a news conference.

"We are proposing not French or other forces from outside but (troops) from within the region here," said Kabila, accusing France of defending Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and forcing him on the people.

French forces based in eastern Zaire intervened in western Rwanda in 1994, setting up safe havens for refugees, most of them Hutus who were fleeing civil war and resprisals for the Hutu genocide of up to one million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.

"We would like the forces of the region to participate to give assurance to the refugees who have to come through the corridors because these refugees fled our soldiers so they need our assurance," Kabila said.
Asked about which troops he wanted to see intervene in eastern Zaire, he said troops from countries that took part in an African summit on the Zaire crisis in Nairobi on Tuesday.
"We have nothing against the French but why are they defending the Mobutu regime, why are they forcing Mobutu on the people," he said in Bukavu, seized by rebel forces more than a week ago.

The Nairobi summit called for a "neutral" force to be set up to protect the 1.2 million refugees uprooted by fighting in eastern Zaire but left the decision to deploy it up to the U.N. Security Council.
Kabila said troops from the region could provide security for humanitarian corridors in government-held areas but those in rebel-held areas would be the responsibility of rebel forces.
"We have to negotiate with the leaders of the region...We are willing to cooperate," said Kabila, who describes himself as the rebel leader but was appointed spokesman by the alliance in October.

He said many former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen and Zairean soldiers were with the refugees and wanted to use them as "cannon fodder" but the rebels wanted them regrouped for humanitarian reasons.
"But we don't want responsibility for the camps because we know that the former soldiers will infiltrate," he added.
He said the rebels controlled all territory running from the town of Uvira in South Kivu province to Goma in North Kivu as well as the Zairean border with Uganda, and would expand the area.
Asked about the possibility of a counter-attack by Zairean forces, he said: "It is inevitable but we don't fear it."
He urged the Zairean people to rise up and join rebels.

"It is for their freedom and this message goes out to the Zairean soldiers as well. They are welcome in our movement. Our ideological base is to free them from the slavery they have been living in," he said.
He said the rebels respected Zaire's territorial integrity and did not want to set up a breakaway state. He denied there were any Rwandan government soldiers in rebel-held areas.
